uncited: Custom Shading Models provide a framework for defining arbitrary illumination calculations within volume rendering and ray-marching pipelines, allowing developers to replace standard analytic lighting with user-defined logic.

This family enables the implementation of specialized effects such as physically based microfacet reflections, directional occlusion, and color-space-specific glow, which are not covered by generic diffuse or specular models.

It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [Distance Color Blending](791-distance-color-blending.md) by operating on explicit geometric data (normals, positions) rather than raw scalar field values, and from [Ambient Occlusion via SDF](1631-ambient-occlusion-via-sdf.md) by allowing full directional light integration rather than just ambient darkening.

The concept of custom shading in volume rendering originated with early libraries like VolPack, which introduced the `vpSetCallback` mechanism allowing users to define per-voxel shading routines instead of relying on fixed lookup tables [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that VolPack offers a second option to 'define a callback routine which will be called to shade each voxel during rendering' by using `vpSetCallback()`. It contrasts this with the alternative of using lookup tables (via `vpSetLookupShader` or custom initialization routines). The claim accurately reflects that VolPack introduced this mechanism for per-voxel shading routines.
